utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to look at the photograph either on the screen in front of you or to your right, and I would ask you if you can identify what is shown in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It's the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First let me ask you, Witness: Do you see anywhere in this photograph the home that you and your husband, Franjo Pavlovic, lived in on 24 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you, Witness, on the photograph to your right, if you would please take the black marker and circle your house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you could draw a line upwards and to the right into the green area and place the number "1" by the house that you have just circled, which was your house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you told us that your husband saw some people outside the window. Can you please -- or do you see the spot on this photograph where those people that your husband saw out of the window were assembled?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please point to that spot where you saw the people assembled, or your husband saw the people assembled.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: This is where he saw Ana Petrovic, here, and this is where the others were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked two X's.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please put the initials "AP" next to the "X" indicating where Ana Petrovic was standing.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It perhaps might be convenient for this photograph to remain for the moment with the witness, as I will ask her to mark additional information on the photograph as we continue with her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did your husband -- what, if anything, did your husband say once he saw these people assembled in the late afternoon, early evening of 24 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He said that something bad was happening, since Ana was crying, something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What, if anything, did your husband do after making this comment?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: My husband and I then went to where these people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately what time was it when you and your husband went out to where the people were standing?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was about 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you recall, what the weather or lighting conditions were at that time on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was a beautiful day. It was sunny.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened after you and your husband joined the small number of people at the location that you've marked with the X on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When we got there, he asked Ana Petrovic, "What's happening? What's going on?" She said that Dedo Suljic had arrived and said that the Mujahedin had gone around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness, when additional people came to this spot in the village?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you remain with your husband at this point in the village?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We got there. I stayed on. And then my husband asked me, he asked Dedo, "Dedo, what's going on?" And he said, "The Mujahedin have gone behind the village," but he didn't know where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did your husband remain at that location, this spot that you've marked with the X on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Dedo's brother, Avdo came, and he told my husband, Franjo, that they should go to Mehurici to see whether the people in the command knew where the Mujahedin had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how far is it from Miletici to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's about 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that they were going to see whether the people in the command knew where the Mujahedin had gone. Do you know which command they were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did your husband in fact go in the direction of Mehurici at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time your husband left, approximately how many people had gathered at the spot marked with the X on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, by the time he left for Mehurici, there were about 30 of us who had gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On April 24th, 1993, do you know approximately how many people lived in the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: There were about 30, 32 or 33 of us. That's how many of us there were when we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, Witness, is it fair to say that virtually all of the villagers of Miletici were gathered at this location at that time on the 24th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what happened after your husband departed in the direction of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When he went off with Avdo Suljic, not more than five minuted had passed when shooting started from all directions. They started shooting at us from all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who was shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Muslim army. The Muslims were shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How do you know it was the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I know because when they started shooting, Dedo climbed up onto a wall of a stables that had been broken down and he started swearing and saying that they shouldn't fire, that Dedo Suljic was there. And he told us that we should flee -- that some of us should flee to Stipo's house and that some of us should take shelter in Ivo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know or do you have any indication as to who Dedo Suljic was talking to when he stood up on the wall and shouted?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: To a Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Dedo Suljic referred to any of the Mujahedin at that time by any names?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told Ramadani not to fire because Dedo Suljic was there. He called his name out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you later saw an individual by the name of Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, Witness, that Dedo Suljic told you that you should flee to Stipo's house. Did you in fact flee to Stipo's house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Looking at the photograph to your right, do you see Stipo Pavlovic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please take the black pen and circle Stipo Pavlovic's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line straight up into the green area and place the number "2" next to the line connecting Stipo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you also indicated that Dedo Suljic said that some of the witnesses should take shelter in Ivo's house. Again, looking at the photograph, do you see the house of Ivo Pavlovic in the photograph to your right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please circle the house of Ivo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line downwards into the green area and place the number "3" next to the house that you've marked or circled as Ivo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown two electronic exhibits, which have been previously admitted into evidence. The first one bearing ERN number 01247883, previously marked as Prosecution Exhibit 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what Prosecution Exhibit 20 is a photograph of.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: This is Stipo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness -- I don't have the photograph on the screen any more. No, the previous one, P20. Witness, you have the photograph in front of you. There is a house with an entrance on the ground floor and above there seem to be two swords drawn on the wall and the word "Jajce" beneath it. What does this emblem represent? What does this sign represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know what the inscription means or what the two crossed swords mean with a white stripe and a blue background? You don't know what this represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. That wasn't written there before. It was written there afterwards. That wasn't on the house before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So with regard to this inscription, you are telling us that it was made at a subsequent date and that the time you were living there, on the 24th of April, that inscription was not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that there is some confusion with regard to the number of the document that we can see. The document we see on the screen is marked P20; whereas, on the list that we were provided with, according to our documents, the document would be P21. If this could just be verified, Mr. President, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, what we have in the archives, in the registry's archives is marked as P21. So when the Prosecution presents a document, a photograph that has already been tendered into evidence, could they mark it correctly. Otherwise, this will give rise to confusion. I would like to thank the Defence for drawing attention to this document. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 22 is now on the screen. Witness, do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please check that it is P22. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, Prosecution Exhibit 22, a photograph, is now visible on the screen in front of you. Do you recognise what is shown in P22?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Ivo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you've told us that you went into the house of Stipo Pavlovic. Do you know or can you tell us the names of any other villagers who fled into Stipo Pavlovic's house on the 24th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Katica Pavlovic, Marija Pavlovic, Tihomir Pavlovic, Vlado Pavlovic, Lucija Pavlovic, Stipo Pavlovic, and Ana Pavlovic, Tihomir's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where in the house of Stipo Pavlovic did these people go?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We went into the corridor and then into a room adjacent to the corridor. Stipo and Lucija Pavlovic remained in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened shortly after you entered the house of Stipo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We entered the house and Stipo shut the door. He said that the Muslims would kill us. They shouted out that they wouldn't, because Dedo said they didn't know where the Mujahedin had gone, they said that they wouldn't do anything to us. He locked the house up and took a rifle. He said that they shouldn't shoot. They said that they would kill us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When they locked the house, the Muslims came to the door. They started banging on the door and they started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did the shooting last?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not for very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened after the shooting stopped?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Stipo then also started shooting in the direction of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time, was Stipo inside his house or outside of his house, when he started shooting?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: In the corridor. He was in the corridor; that's where Stipo was, in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did Stipo shoot from the corridor of his house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Not for very long, and then he stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened after Stipo Pavlovic stopped shooting?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When he stopped shooting, the Muslims broke the door down and they threw a grenade in. It must have been a grenade. Something exploded in the corridor. There was smoke, then as if a tyre had been burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the people in Stipo Pavlovic's house when this explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We screamed and we were crying. Lucija started crying at the same time and said that she, Lucija, had been wounded, that Stipo had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened after Lucija made these comments?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when Lucija said this, we were crying and two Muslim soldiers entered the room we were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what these soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: One was wearing a black T-shirt, and the other one had a police insignia on his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were either of these individuals wearing any kind of insignia that -- by which you were able to identify the organisation or military units that they might have been affiliated with?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No. But when I went outside, I saw that someone had a band around his arm and it said "BiH." There were three letters. And I didn't see any other insignia. I didn't notice anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if the soldier who is -- the two soldiers who entered Stipo Pavlovic's house, do you know if they were local Muslims or if they were foreign Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: One was a Mujahedin for sure, since he didn't know how to speak. He started shooting at a person and he shouted out, "Outside. Outside," because he didn't know our language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once these soldiers entered Stipo Pavlovic's house, what did the group of people in that house do?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we went outside. We fled outside, because he was shooting and shouted out and said we should go outside. We went outside, because in the corridor we saw Stipo on the ground and Lucija was crying by his side. We jumped over Stipo and went outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where in the village did you go? When you say you went outside, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We went to a place between Stipo and Ivo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the usher return the photograph, the aerial photograph that the witness was previously marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, in the photograph to your right, do you see the location where you went when you exited Stipo Pavlovic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness take the pointer and point to the location where the individuals who had been in Stipo Pavlovic's house assembled after they left that house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please take the black pen, place an "X" and circle the "X" at the location where you gathered after leaving Stipo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, after the group assembled at the location with the circled X, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When we came out there, then the people who had been in Ivo Pavlovic's house came out too, and they started cursing us because we had apparently killed a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, Witness, "they started cursing us," who was it that was cursing you at that point?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The people who had been in Ivo Pavlovic's house, where did they go once they left Ivo's house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They came to the same spot as we had gathered at, those of us who had been in Stipo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were gathered at the spot that you have placed an X on and circled? How many villagers were at that spot at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: There were about 29 or 30 of us, because my husband was not with us then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that point in time, Witness, do you know where your husband was?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He was with Avdo Suljic, because he said that they were going to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to the group of 29 or 30 of you at the location with the circled X.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim soldiers told us that we should go to our houses and collect weapons and bring them there, because those people who don't bring weapons would be immediately executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how many Muslim soldiers did you see at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you exactly, but there may have been 15 to 20 of them or -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if of these 15 to 20 there were local Muslims or foreign Muslims or a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Both. There were both. Both of them were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe the type of clothing worn by these 15 to 20 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage military clothes. But not all of them. They were not all in military uniforms. Some were in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that the Muslim soldiers said that you should go to your houses. In fact, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe how it was that you went to your houses.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I set off towards my house, and Ramadani set off with me. And when I reached a point between Ivo's house and my own, there's a small stream there. I was very frightened, and he pushed me with his rifle but he said, "I won't kill you. I won't kill you," but he wasn't speaking properly. He wasn't speaking our language properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you in fact return to your home with the man you've identified as Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you do at your house and how long were you there?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I reached the house with Ramadani. He was behind me. I found the rifle that we had received. And I said, "Should I bring the ammunition as well?" And he said I didn't need the ammunition, just the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in your house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: A couple of minutes, just to pick up the weapon, and then I went out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left your house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I was between Ivo's and Stipo's house, because that is where they had spread out some canvas, military canvas, and they told us to put the rifles on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the other villagers from Miletici again congregated at the spot where you drew the X with the circle?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because those who had weapons went back to their homes to bring them and came back with them to their same spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time it was when you returned to that spot and placed the rifle on the canvas between Ivo's and Stipo's houses?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. Maybe an hour or two had gone by. About an hour. I think that's how long it took to do all this. It was about 7.00, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain at that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Not long. They started cursing us for killing this one person, and the man who had come into the house and who had shouted, "Out. Get out. Get out," he said that all of us should be slaughtered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you then taken or removed to a different location?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But then they tied us up. And when they tied up our hands behind our backs, then Avdo brought my husband back to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was your husband brought to the location where you and the other villagers were gathered?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because Avdo came and said, "I am Avdo Suljic." And then this Muslim came up to him and told him to go back. Then my husband followed him, and then this one came up to him and said, "You, Franjo, you go back. You are not a Muslim."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what happened after those words were said?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Avdo went home, and Franjo stayed with us. Then they tied us up, and then they separated the men from the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many men were separated from the rest of you, the rest of the group?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They took away my husband, Franjo, Tihomir, Vlado, and Anto when we brought the weapons. Then one of them raised his hand and said that there should be five of them. And then this other one said that -- pointed to the house where Stipo had been killed, and then they said it was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The four men that you've just identified, Franjo, Tihomir, Vlado, and Anto, you told us that they took them away. Where did they take them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They separated them from us and they ordered them to kneel down in front of Ivo's house, Franjo, Tihomir, and Vlado. However, Anto was taken away. I don't know where they took him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did you then remain after seeing the men taken away and placed in a kneeling position?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe 5 or 10 minutes, because they were separated from us, ordered to kneel down, while the rest of us were ordered to move on towards Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you in fact then proceed towards Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Dedo Suljic and Akif went with us, but they were not tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How many people were in the group that was tied and taken towards Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, about 25, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I'm about to go into a different area, and I do believe it's close to the normal recess time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are quite right. We are going to adjourn now for technical reasons for 25 minutes, and we will resume at five to 6.00. Can the Prosecution tell me how much more time they need for the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will certainly review my notes during the break, but I would anticipate between 10 and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 10 to 15 minutes? Would three-quarters of an hour be sufficient for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For Defence counsel for General Hadzihasanovic, that will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. President. Microphone. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Let us have the witness brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give the floor once again to the Prosecution to complete their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, just before the break, you told us that the group of about 25 people from Miletici was marched in the direction of Mehurici. Did you in fact go to the village of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you do or what did the group do upon arriving in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Mehurici, some people were yelling that we should be taken to the school, and another group that we should be taken to Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who was -- you say "some people were yelling." Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were these people yelling?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were shouting that we should be taken to Poljanice, and others that we should be taken to the school, because it looked like a celebration there. There were so many people at Mehurici. Some people were saying, "Let them go. They're not to blame for anything." Others were cursing us. We didn't really pay attention as to what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know -- when there was references to the school, do you know which school these people were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The school for children in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know on April 24th, 1993 to what use that school was being made?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: While children were still going to school, they went there. And when school stopped, the Muslim army used the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you in fact go to the school in Mehurici, or did you go to Poljanice?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No. We went to Poljanice, to a Serb house. We were taken there. The men were taken to the stable, and us, we were put into the basement of a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was there anyone in the basement of the house when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: There were two Serb women there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in that house? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there three, four, five hours. I don't know. Maybe until after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where did you go after you left that house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We went to Luka, where the Muslims were, because Ribo Suljo came to say allegedly that he had got us released from the Muslim army, and then he took us to Luka, to some Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the Muslim houses in Luka?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached the Muslim houses at Luka, it was Sunday. And then Monday we returned to our homes in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How did you return to Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We left because the Muslims at Luka were saying that we shouldn't go to Miletici because there were Muslim soldiers there. But we still decided ourselves to go to our village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How many of you decided to go to the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: All of us. There were about 25 or 26 of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How did you get from Luka to Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We went on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is the approximate distance from Luka to Miletici and how long did it take to walk there that day?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: About 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately how far is it, in terms of distance?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: If you take a shortcut, it's not so far, about 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately what time on the morning of Monday, 26 April 1993 did you arrive back in the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was about 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you arrived in Miletici, did you see anyone that you knew upon your arrival?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I saw Dedo Suljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you say anything to Dedo Suljic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He asked us why we had come to the village and who had let us come. And I asked him what he was doing there anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you tell Dedo Suljic why you had returned to the village?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We said we had come to see where our people were, those who had been killed, who had been left behind in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that point, did you know that people had been killed in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Because UNPROFOR went to Miletici on Sunday, and on their way back they told us that our people, who had stayed behind in Miletici, had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Upon arrival that morning in Miletici, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived there, I asked Sreco Pavlovic, "Where are our dead?" He told me they were in Ivo's house but not in Stipo's house, that they had been transferred to Ivo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you in fact on that morning go to Ivo Pavlovic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you saw when you entered Ivo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When I entered the house, I saw five dead bodies wrapped in blankets. I started uncovering them. The first was Tihomir. I saw it wasn't my husband, and I went on. Then the second one was Stipo Pavlovic. When I reached the third person, I saw, when I uncovered him, that it was my husband, and then I didn't go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that this may be difficult, but can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the condition of your husband's body when you uncovered it on that morning.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: My husband was on his stomach, and his head wasn't facing down but to the left. In any case, I couldn't see his face. I saw blood round his neck and a wound on his back and his hands were tied behind the back -- his back. I took off his watch and wanted to turn him around but Sreco came in and told me to get out. "What was I looking for?" He said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see any other unusual marks or indications of any specific types of wounds on your husband's body?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: At the time I didn't, but later on, when my brother came to Nova Bila, when I saw the photographs, I saw on the photographs that there were other wounds on him, because I wanted to turn him around but I couldn't. I didn't have the strength to do that at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what other wounds you saw on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that he had a shot next to his eye, that his eye had come out, that he had a wound on his chest, and that he had knife wounds on his legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you now if you could turn again to the photograph on the ELMO to your right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Prosecution whether they intend to show the photograph of her husband to the witness. If there is no challenge regarding his condition, it is the opinion of the Chamber that it is not really necessary to refresh memories of this personal drama by showing photographs of the witness's husband, as this is not challenged by the Defence, everyone agrees that her husband was killed. Does the Prosecution wish to show the lady, who is also an indirect victim, the photograph of her husband?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution had originally intended to do so. However, in light of events transpiring with respect to a previous witness, the Prosecution was not going to show those photos. We were going to move on to a final series of questions concerning the aerial photograph of Miletici, which is on the ELMO to the witness's right, and that would then conclude the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will be showing her an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which is the same photograph that she's previously made several markings on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, on the photograph to your right, do you see the house where Tihomir Pavlovic lived?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please take the black marker and circle the house where Tihomir Pavlovic lived.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please place the number "4" next to the circle that you've just drawn on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, on the photograph, do you see the house of Anto Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please circle the house of Anto Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please place the number "5" next to the circle of the house of Anto Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the house where Vlado Pavlovic lived in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please circle that house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please place the number "6" next to the house that you've circled where Vlado Pavlovic lived.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you please tell us who else lived in the house marked number 6 with Vlado Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: His parents, his sister, Marija, and his sister, Katica, and his brother, Filip, who was in Switzerland at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: His sister Katica subsequently married and is no longer known as Katica Pavlovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what her name -- her married name is, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you please tell the Trial Chamber who was older, Vlado Pavlovic or Katica Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were twins.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that the Prosecution wants to tender this aerial photograph into evidence, a photograph which has been authenticated. Witness, could you mark your first and last name on this photograph, today's date, and could you sign the document. It's the 12th of January, 2004 today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you sign the document or put your name on it, mark it with your name or sign it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could you show the Defence this document. And the accused as well. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit number will be P32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has been tendered into evidence, and the exhibit number is P32. Before the Defence takes the floor for its cross-examination, I have two brief questions that I would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you mentioned two persons that you met when you were arrested and taken from village to village. You spoke about Ribo Suljo, who, if I have understood this correctly from your answers to the Prosecution, was the person who intervened to release you in a certain sense. According to you, Ribo Suljo, what was his position? Was he a soldier, a civilian? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what he was, but I think he was a teacher in the school. But whether he was someone in the army, I don't know, since this is not knowledge I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Was he dressed in civilian clothes or in a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see him, because it was dark. It was night-time, and I couldn't see him well. I did see him, but in fact I didn't pay any attention to what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The second person that you mentioned when you were returning to Miletici is a person who seemed to be surprised to see you. You spoke about Mr. Dedo Suljic. I would like to ask you the same question about this person. Did he have some sort of official position?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No. He was an elderly man. He didn't have duties of any kind, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And again, I would like to ask you: Was he wearing civilian clothes or was he wearing military clothing?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He was dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Witness. We have another 35 minutes for the cross-examination. The Defence may now take the floor for its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Pavlovic, good evening.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and I represent General Hadzihasanovic. I would like to ask you to answer several questions, if you know the answers to my questions. When asked by the Prosecution, you said that you arrived in the village of Miletici in 1982, after you had got married. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that time, up until today, the 24th of April, 1993 you lived in Gornji Miletici continually; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The inhabitants in Gornji Miletici are on the whole of Croatian nationality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second hamlet of the village of Miletici there were four families. The brothers Suljic lived there, Dedo, Avdo, and Akif Suljic. They were Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Pavlovic, on several occasions up until now you have spoken about the event in the police station in Busovaca and the last statement you gave was to the OTP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was in Zagreb, to investigators. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1992, the attacks of the Serbian forces from the area of Mount Vlasic directed against the wider area of the villages of Mehurici and Miletici commenced, but your village was never hit; is that correct? Your village was never affected.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to those conflicts, your relations with the Muslims from Donji Miletici were very good -- in spite of these conflicts, your relations with the Muslims were very good; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the day mentioned when your village was attacked, you said that your husband had spent the entire day in the field, ploughing there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout that period of time, while he was in the field, he was with Avdo Suljic, who was a friend of his.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Prosecution, you said that at some point in time at the end of 1992 and 1993 you noticed that there were foreigners in that area, the so-called Mujahedin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were very different from the local inhabitants. They spoke a foreign language, and those who spoke our language or knew a little of our language had an accent, so everyone knew they were foreigners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of them had Arafat-style scarves, head scarves, and a long beard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you had good relations with your neighbours, but because of the conflicts in the wider area between the army -- the BH army and the HVO, towards the beginning of 1993 people started going on guard duty in your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Muslim neighbours were members of the BH army and the men who were fit for military service from your village were in the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were part of the Frankopan Brigade, whose command was located in Guca Gora; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Prosecution, you also said that on that day, the 24th of April, 1993, at about 6.00 in the evening, Dedo, Akif, and Avdo Suljic came to the village to warn you about the presence of the Mujahedin in the immediate vicinity of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, they were hoping that the Mujahedin would not attack the village and they told you that there was no need to be afraid.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if that's not contained in the testimony, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that point, they said that they were prepared to defend you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They said that before. They said if something happened to them, it would happen to us too. And on that day they said that we shouldn't spread panic. They said that they wouldn't do anything to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time you also said - and I'm asking you to confirm this - you said that your husband and his friend, Avdo Suljic, went to the BH army command in Mehurici in order to inform them about what was happening. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He called my husband to go to Mehurici to see if they knew anything about where the Mujahedin had gone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, before they returned - and you have already described this in detail - shooting broke out. They started shooting at you in the village.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dedo Suljic, as you said, called Ramadani by name and asked them to stop shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, his shouting had no effect. There was no response. And the shooting did not stop. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because while they were shouting, he said that we should go into Stipo and Ivo's house. We did so, and they remained outside. Dedo remained outside, as well as Akif.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While the shooting was going on, only Stipo Pavlovic returned fire from his house, which is where you were too; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the attackers had broken down the door and thrown a grenade in, Stipo Pavlovic was killed and his wife, Lucija, was wounded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were coming outside of the house, you noticed that one of the attackers had been killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recognised the person as an inhabitant of Mehurici, and it was known that he was a follower of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when we went out, it must have been his brother, and someone shouted out, "Why did you kill him?" I knew him. I asked him where is he from. He said, "You don't know. You couldn't know." Akif's wife said that he had -- that if he had entered the house, he would have killed all of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have already said, there were some foreign soldiers, some Mujahedin, in this group who spoke a foreign language and had long beards and there were also local Muslims among them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The local people had camouflage paint and some were wearing ski masks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, some of them had some sort of paint or mud on them, but I didn't see any of them wearing masks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You noticed that one of the attackers was wearing a blue police uniform, which is usually worn by the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't have a police uniform but he had a band on his arm and it said "The police" on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by Mr. President, you said that Dedo Suljic was wearing civilian clothes. Is it correct to say that the other Suljic brothers were wearing civilian clothes on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that Lucija, who had been wounded, asked for help at one point in time and Akif Suljic went to aid her?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that point, one of the Mujahedin hit him in the head with the butt of his rifle and he started bleeding; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you had been tied up and taken in the direction of Mehurici, Dedo and Akif Suljic were taken with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But they hadn't tied them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were still in the village, you said that this person called Ramadan escorted you to your house so that you could take the rifle from the house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He could speak our language to a certain extent, but he had an accent and it was quite clear that he was a foreigner; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, he in fact issued orders to all the others and it was clear to you that he was in command of the group that had attacked the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was certainly like that, because Dedo called him out by name, so he must have been in charge of that group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were taken to Mehurici, they took you to Poljice, as you said --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: To Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To Poljanice, which is where these foreign Mujahedin were also present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that at that point you were separated from the men and you remained in the cellar until around midnight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by the Presiding Judge, you said that Ribo Suljo, who was a teacher, negotiated in order to obtain your release and he managed to have you released around midnight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ribo Suljo was a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The BH army members, Ribo Suljo, and the police from Mehurici managed to get you a bus -- get you on a bus, which took you to the village of Luka.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Luka is a village -- is the village in which Ribo Suljo lived, and he found accommodation for you in his grandparents' house, which was adjacent to his house.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that was his father's father. He took us to his own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They protected you that night to prevent any other incidents perpetrated by the Mujahedin from occurring; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to what he said, yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to Mr. Dixon, does the Prosecution wish to intervene? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No. Thank you. I'll be brief. There are no questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for you, Madam, to clarify a point which the Judges have in their minds in view of your statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your opinion, Madam, the people who attacked your village, those you described as Mujahedin in your opinion - though of course you're not a military expert but you're a witness of fact and you saw them - these people, these foreigners, in your opinion, to the best of your knowledge, were they a part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I think that they did belong to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what you believe, but without having any additional elements to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They were with the Muslims, so I consider them to have been together. I can't say with certainty when I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So according to you, the local Muslims were integrated within the BH army.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I hesitate to intervene at this point. Clearly the Prosecution is fully aware of the right of the Chamber to ask questions of the witness at any time, except for this particular question, because it is a question that asks for an opinion, and I would like to convey the position of the Defence concerning questions of opinion from the witness, because such questions may be put again. And we would like from the beginning to present the position of the Defence on this matter. With your leave, Mr. President, I will be brief. The position of the Defence regarding an opinion given by an ordinary witness is the following: An ordinary witness, as opposed to an expert witness, cannot give an opinion in his testimony because it is not reliable, in the first place; and furthermore, it can lead the Chamber -- it can mislead the Chamber. It is -- it cannot be precise. And it is not -- it does not rely on any base which evidently calls in question its probative value. A fact witness takes the place of a judge of fact, who should on the basis of the facts presented to him, on the basis of what he is told by witnesses, without any external aid to be able to make a judgement. A testimony of an opinion, as you certainly know, is allowed only in the case of expert witnesses, because an expert witness had special expertise which can be of assistance to the Chamber when addressing a point. If we look at the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we see clearly the distinction that needs to be made between a fact witness and an expert witness, and this distinction is found in Rule 90(C). The fact witness, as opposed to an expert witness, should not be influenced by other testimony. So that is the Rule 90(C), which implicitly recognises that the testimony of a fact witness should only be limited to what he saw and heard himself and should not be an opinion based on other testimony or on other facts. Furthermore, the Rules of Procedure also envisages a special regime regarding the proof offered by an expert witness. A special regime in Rule 94 bis regarding the testimony of an expert witness says that "This opinion can be presented only by a qualified person and one with an expertise that the Chamber does not have." So it would not be logical to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. take so many precautions, to have so many Rules - 90 and 94 bis of the Rules - indicating that an expert must have certain qualities to be able to give an opinion; and on the other hand, to allow a fact witness, without any verification of competence or qualifications to pronounce an opinion on a fact that the Chamber can make an opinion without assistance. And the question is how such a witness could give an opinion that would have probative value. The jurisprudence of the Tribunal also distinguishes -- makes a distinction between these two categories of witnesses. And I refer you to a decision in this connection. I will quote it in English. [In English] "This is a motion by the Prosecution to allow the investigators to follow the trial during the testimonies of witnesses." [Interpretation] It was in the Delalic case, IT-86-21-T, for trial; in the Celebici case in March 1997. The doctrine also establishes a clear distinction between the testimony of an expert and the testimony of a fact witness. By way of an example, in Anne Marie Larosa, in her manual, Criminal National Jurisdiction tells us that there are two types of witnesses, fact witnesses, ordinary witnesses who convey facts of which they have personal knowledge, and an expert witness who makes comparisons in order to make a precise opinion regarding a particular fact. The Manual of Quebec also makes a distinction and says "An expert witness is not prevented from testifying about facts that he has no personal knowledge of." So -- "however, a fact witness relies mostly on facts he has personal knowledge of." In conclusion, Mr. President, considering the problem of reliability and probative value to be given to an opinion of a fact witness, and in view of the distinction that exists between evidence introduced by a fact witness and an expert witness, the Defence, with respect, submits that an opinion coming from a fact witness could never -- should never be accepted. I will conclude quickly. The question put to the witness is a key question in the current case. This question is one that many witnesses will be testifying about. This is a question that is of key significance, and it is normal to tend to ask a witness whether there was any link between the Mujahedin and the BH army. But, Mr. President, with due respect, it is only the Chamber itself that will be able to answer that question, based on what the witnesses will tell you on the basis of their own personal knowledge. Therefore, I would ask, Mr. President, with all due respect, that it be redacted from the transcript of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor now to the Prosecution. We have another ten minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I certainly won't need ten minutes, Mr. President. Rule 89(C) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence is quite clear: "A Chamber may admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value." The Prosecution would submit that the question or questions put by the Bench to the witness are not so much of a character as to be considered opinion evidence but, rather, is evidence of conclusions that the witness may have reached based on things that she observed. And it is not at all unlike a situation where a witness might testify that it rained last night not because the witness was up all night and actually watched the raindrops hitting the pavement but because in the morning the witness noticed that there were puddles everywhere which weren't there the day before. In the event the Defence would like to more fully address and brief this issue, the Prosecution would be happy to respond to written submissions or, if those would be helpful to the Chamber, we would be more than happy to assist the Chamber in terms of briefing this issue in writing. I should also note just for the future - and I'm sure it's simply an oversight on behalf of the Defence - but the Prosecution view would be any time where lengthy legal submissions are made orally, the Prosecution would submit it's certainly more proper for the witness to be removed from the courtroom prior to such oral legal submissions being made. That's really all the Prosecution has to submit at this time, Your Honour. But again, if it would be helpful to the Chamber, we can certainly more fully brief the issue. But the Prosecution would submit at this time that if the Chamber deems it to be relevant and to have probative value, that it certainly falls more in lines with any other type of perhaps circumstantial or conclusionary-type evidence and not so much an opinion. And of course, as the Defence correctly points out, will be the ultimate arbiter of this key issue in the case. But the Prosecution would submit that the line of questioning put to the witness by Your Honour certainly falls within the scope of both relevance and probative value, in light of what the witness testified that she actually saw and the conclusions that she drew, based on her own observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We will rule tomorrow morning at the beginning of the hearing whether, in view of our question and the response given, whether it should be mentioned in the transcript or redacted. All precautions have been taken to inform the witness that she was not an expert witness, and she was asked to answer a question to the best of her knowledge on the basis of what she saw and that what she told us was her conclusion, because she noted that the local Muslims were integrated within the ABiH, and as the foreigners were with the local Muslims, she came to the conclusion that they were integrated within the ABiH. Will you please refer to the transcript, when the witness indicated that the local Muslims were a part of the ABiH. But we will rule about this tomorrow regarding this particular point, which is an important point, and the Chamber, of course, has listened to Mr. Bourgon with great attention, who had already prepared his intervention, having studied the matter in depth, knowing that the question would arise. So you will have our decision tomorrow in response to the question raised, the particular question raised. Within the framework of questions that we have heard, has the Prosecution any re-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.
